claim: MGA is mutated or deleted in 53 of 507 (10%) lung adenocarcinoma patients in the TCGA dataset.
source: Focusing on MGA, we note that it is mutated or deleted in 53 of 507 (10%) lung adenocarcinoma patients (TCGA)
evidence: The claim is directly supported by data from the TCGA database as stated in the manuscript text.

claim: MGA is mutated or deleted in 233 of 3696 (6%) patients sequenced through the GENIE project.
source: in 233 of 3696 (6%) patients sequenced through the GENIE project (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by data from the GENIE project and referenced in a figure.

claim: The majority of MGA mutations in lung adenocarcinoma are truncating mutations.
source: The majority of MGA mutations in lung adenocarcinoma are truncating mutations (Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Approximately 25% of MGA mutations in the TCGA LUAD dataset are homozygous.
source: with approximately 25% homozygosity in the TCGA LUAD dataset, suggestive of selection for inactivating mutations in tumorigenesis
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA data.

claim: Low levels of MGA in lung adenocarcinoma significantly correlate with decreased overall survival.
source: In addition, low levels of MGA in lung adenocarcinoma significantly correlate with decreased overall survival (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Győrffy et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in a figure and cited from a published study.

claim: There was a significant decrease in survival in Kras G12D mice receiving sgMga when compared to mice receiving empty vector.
source: There was a significant decrease in survival in Kras G12D mice receiving sgMga when compared to mice receiving the lentiCRISPRv2 vector containing Cre and Cas9 but lacking sgMga (referred to herein as 'empty' vector; Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental survival data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Tumors from sgMga-treated mice exhibited a higher proliferation index as ascertained by Ki67 staining when compared to mice infected with empty vector controls.
source: Tumors from sgMga-treated mice exhibited a higher proliferation index as ascertained by Ki67 staining when compared to mice infected with empty vector controls (Figure 1C,D)
evidence: The claim is supported by Ki67 staining data shown in figures.

claim: Sequencing of tumors confirmed the presence of indels predicted to result in premature truncation in 75% (6/8) tumors isolated from sgMga-treated mice.
source: Sequencing of tumors confirmed the presence of indels predicted to result in premature truncation in 75% (6/8) tumors isolated from sgMga-treated mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data from tumors.

claim: There is a significant co-occurrence of genomic alterations in MGA and TP53 in lung adenocarcinoma patients.
source: Intriguingly, TCGA and GENIE data revealed that there is a significant co-occurrence of genomic alterations in MGA and TP53 in lung adenocarcinoma patients (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA and GENIE data shown in a figure.

claim: At 3 months after intratracheal instillation of lentiCRISPRv2cre, KP-sgMga mice had a substantially higher tumor burden when compared to KP mice similarly treated with control vector.
source: At 3 months after intratracheal instillation of lentiCRISPRv2cre, KP-sgMga mice had a substantially higher tumor burden when compared to KP mice similarly treated with control vector (Figure 1E,F)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: KP-sgMga mice had an overall increase in number of tumors and tumor grade upon Mga inactivation.
source: This was accompanied by an overall increase in number of tumors and tumor grade upon Mga inactivation (Figure 1G,H)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: sgMga tumors had an increased proportion of Ki67+ tumor cells when compared to controls.
source: Immunostaining revealed that sgMga tumors had an increased proportion of Ki67+ tumor cells when compared to controls (Figure 1I,J)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in figures.

claim: sgMga tumors had increased vasculature as evidenced by MECA32 staining when compared to controls.
source: Consistent with increase in tumor grade, sgMga tumors had increased vasculature (as evidenced by MECA32 staining) when compared to controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G,H)
evidence: The claim is supported by MECA32 staining data shown in figures.

claim: A substantial decrease in MGA protein levels was observed in most KP-sgMga cell lines.
source: A substantial decrease in MGA protein levels was observed in most KP-sgMga cell lines (Figure 1K,L, Figure 1—figure supplement 1I)
evidence: The claim is supported by protein level data shown in figures.

claim: Ectopic expression of MGA in KP-sgMga lines impaired proliferation.
source: We confirmed that KP-sgMga lines are dependent on the inactivation of Mga as ectopic expression of MGA in KP-sgMga lines impaired proliferation (Figure 1M,N)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data on proliferation shown in figures.

claim: Several meiotic genes, such as Stag3, Sox30, and Tdrd1, previously reported to be directly regulated by MGA-PRC1.6 in ES and germline cells, exhibited a striking increase in expression in Mga-inactivated cells.
source: Despite the heterogeneity, Mga-inactivated cells exhibited a striking increase in expression of several meiotic genes, such as Stag3, Sox30, and Tdrd1, previously reported to be directly regulated by MGA-PRC1.6 in ES and germline cells (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1a; Suzuki et al., 2016)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data and citation to a previous study.

claim: Ccnd1 levels were elevated in sgMga tumors compared to control.
source: Consistent with our Ki67 data, Ccnd1 levels were elevated in sgMga tumors compared to control (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1a)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in a figure.

claim: Several metabolic pathways and a subset of MYC-regulated genes were upregulated in sgMga tumors.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis revealed that several metabolic pathways and a subset of MYC-regulated genes were also upregulated in sgMga tumors, indicating that MGA represses MYC targets, similar to repression by MXDs seen in other tumor models (Figure 2B; Yang and Hurlin, 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by gene set enrichment analysis and citation to a previous study.

claim: Inactivation of Mga led to the downregulation of genes involved in anti-tumor responses, such as NK cell markers and interferon signaling genes.
source: However, inactivation of Mga led to the downregulation of genes involved in anti-tumor responses, such as NK cell markers and interferon signaling genes (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in figures.

claim: Several ncPRC1.6 complex repressed germ cell related transcripts, including Stag3, were highly upregulated in KP cells lacking MGA.
source: Despite the differences in genetic background (Kras vs. KP), several ncPRC1.6 complex repressed germ cell related transcripts, including Stag3, were highly upregulated in KP cells lacking MGA (Figure 2D, Supplementary file 1b), similar to Kras-sgMga tumors
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in a figure.

claim: An upregulation of pro-invasive genes such as Podxl2, Gpc2, Snai2, and Itga1 was observed in KP cells lacking MGA.
source: In addition, we also observed an upregulation of pro-invasive genes such as Podxl2, Gpc2, Snai2, and Itga1 (Figure 2D)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in a figure.

claim: Epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) and TGF-beta signaling were amongst the most significantly enriched pathways in sgMga KP cells.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis revealed that epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) and TGF-beta signaling were amongst the most significantly enriched pathways in sgMga KP cells (Figure 2E)
evidence: The claim is supported by gene set enrichment analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Genes upregulated in sgMga KP cells correlated significantly with those upregulated upon MYC, E2F4, and TWIST1 overexpression in other systems.
source: Intriguingly, genes upregulated in sgMga KP cells correlated significantly with those upregulated upon MYC, E2F4, and TWIST1 overexpression in other systems (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in a figure.

claim: There was a significant correlation with genes reported to be upregulated upon PCGF6 knockdown or MYC overexpression.
source: In addition, there was also a significant correlation with genes reported to be upregulated upon PCGF6 knockdown or MYC overexpression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Full-length MGA or MGA fragments (aa967–1300 and aa2153–2856) interact with several repressive molecules and complexes including members of the ncPRC1.6 complex such as RING2 and L3MBTL2.
source: We confirmed that full-length MGA or MGA fragments (aa967–1300 and aa2153–2856) interact with several repressive molecules and complexes (protein prophet score > 0.9). These include members of the ncPRC1.6 complex such as RING2 and L3MBTL2 (Figure 3A)
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in a figure.

claim: MGA associated with WDR5, RBBP5, ASH2L, and DPY30 (members of the chromatin modifier MLL-WRAD complex) and HDACs 1 and 2.
source: In addition, MGA also associated with WDR5, RBBP5, ASH2L, and DPY30 (members of the chromatin modifier MLL-WRAD complex) and HDACs 1 and 2 (Figure 3A)
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in a figure.

claim: Mga loss resulted in decreased protein levels of E2F6, PCGF6, and L3MBTL2 despite equivalent mRNA levels.
source: Mga loss resulted in decreased protein levels of E2F6, PCGF6, and L3MBTL2 (Figure 3B–E) despite equivalent mRNA levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by protein and mRNA level data shown in figures.

claim: MAX levels remain unchanged upon Mga loss.
source: whereas MAX levels remain unchanged (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by protein and mRNA level data shown in figures.

claim: Decreased E2F6, L3MBTL2, and PCGF6 protein levels were confirmed in MGA mutant human non-small cell lung cancer lines H2291 and Lou-NH-91 when compared to wild-type lines such as NCI-H1975, NCI-H23, and 91T.
source: We further confirmed decreased E2F6, L3MBTL2, and PCGF6 protein levels in MGA mutant human non-small cell lung cancer lines H2291 and Lou-NH-91 when compared to wild-type lines such as NCI-H1975, NCI-H23, and 91T (Figure 3F–I)
evidence: The claim is supported by protein level data shown in figures.

claim: The region encompassing aa 967–1300 interacts with L3MBTL2 and several other proteins.
source: Our initial mass spectrometric analysis of immunoprecipitates using fragments of MGA in 293FT cells revealed that the region encompassing aa 967–1300 interacts with L3MBTL2 (an obligate component of PRC1.6) and several other proteins (Figure 3A)
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in a figure.

claim: The region aa 1043–1084 includes a conserved domain of unknown function (DUF4801).
source: Interrogation of protein domain databases revealed that this region includes a conserved domain of unknown function (DUF4801, located at aa 1043–1084)
evidence: The claim is supported by interrogation of protein domain databases.

claim: L3MBTL2 preferentially associates with wild-type MGA as compared with MGA∆DUF.
source: Figure 4A shows preferential association of L3MBTL2 with wild-type MGA as compared with MGA∆DUF
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in a figure.

claim: Multiple truncating mutations in MGA occur within the AA1003–1304 region surrounding DUF4801 in lung adenocarcinomas.
source: Focusing on lung adenocarcinomas, TCGA sequencing data revealed that multiple truncating mutations in MGA occur within the AA1003–1304 region surrounding DUF4801 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B)
evidence: The claim is supported by TCGA sequencing data shown in figures.

claim: Addback of MGA∆DUF had no effect on proliferation of KP cells whereas expression of WT MGA led to a significant decrease in proliferation.
source: To study the functional importance of this region, we ectopically expressed either the WT or MGA∆DUF versions in two different sgMga mouse KP lines and observed that addback of MGA∆DUF had no effect on proliferation of KP cells whereas expression of WT MGA led to a significant decrease in proliferation (Figure 4B–D)
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation data shown in figures.

claim: An increase in L3MBTL2 protein levels was observed upon wild type MGA addition but not upon MGA∆DUF expression in the human MGA mutant lung squamous cell line LOU-NH-91.
source: We then transduced the human MGA mutant lung squamous cell line LOU-NH-91 with full-length MGA or MGA∆DUF and observed an increase in L3MBTL2 protein levels upon wild type MGA addition but not upon MGA∆DUF expression (Figure 4E)
evidence: The claim is supported by protein level data shown in a figure.

claim: MYC levels and, to a lesser extent, MAX levels decreased in MGA and MGA∆DUF over-expressing cells.
source: MYC levels and, to a lesser extent, MAX levels decreased in MGA and MGA∆DUF over-expressing cells, suggesting feedback regulation within the network (Figure 4E)
evidence: The claim is supported by protein level data shown in a figure and inference about feedback regulation.

claim: Full-length MGA addback resulted in a drastic reduction in cell number, while MGA∆DUF expression led to only a mild impairment in proliferation.
source: In contrast to full-length MGA addback, which resulted in a drastic reduction in cell number, MGA∆DUF expression led to only a mild impairment in proliferation suggesting that the association of ncPRC1.6 is unlikely to account for all of MGA's antiproliferative activity (Figure 4F)
evidence: The claim is supported by cell proliferation data shown in a figure.

claim: MGA, MAX, E2F6, and L3MBTL2 bind several thousand promoters in MGA-expressing KP tumor cells.
source: MGA, MAX, E2F6, and L3MBTL2 were seen to bind several thousand promoters in MGA-expressing KP tumor cells suggesting that the PRC1.6 complex plays a broad role in tumor cell gene expression (Supplementary file 1c)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data.

claim: 85% of MAX, and nearly all L3MBTL2 and E2F6 binding loci, are also occupied by MGA.
source: Strikingly, 85% of MAX, and nearly all L3MBTL2 and E2F6 binding loci, are also occupied by MGA (Figure 5A)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in a figure.

claim: A marked reduction in L3MBTL2 and E2F6 binding was noted in KP-sgMga cells, while overall MAX and MYC genomic occupancy was only modestly affected.
source: Moreover, we noted a marked reduction in L3MBTL2 and E2F6 binding in KP-sgMga cells, while overall MAX and MYC genomic occupancy was only modestly affected (Figure 5B,C)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in figures.

claim: MGA binding is observed to the majority of genes significantly upregulated and downregulated upon MGA loss.
source: Regarding altered gene expression, we observe MGA binding to the majority of genes significantly upregulated and downregulated upon MGA loss (Figure 5D)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq and RNA-seq data shown in a figure.

claim: Significant enrichment of both MGA and ncPRC1.6 subunits (i.e. L3MBTL2 and E2F6) binding was detected at Stag3/GPC2 and Podxl2 promoters, which are upregulated in sgMga-KP cells.
source: Focusing on several key genes previously associated with MGA function, we detected significant enrichment of both MGA and ncPRC1.6 subunits (i.e. L3MBTL2 and E2F6) binding at Stag3/GPC2 and Podxl2 promoters, which are upregulated in sgMga-KP cells (Figure 5E,F)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in figures.

claim: MYC binding is augmented at Stag3 and Podxl2 in sgMga cells, in contrast to decreased occupancy of L3MBTL2 and E2F6 at the same loci.
source: For example, MYC binding is augmented at Stag3 and Podxl2 in sgMga cells, in contrast to decreased occupancy of L3MBTL2 and E2F6 at the same loci (Figure 5E,F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in figures.

claim: Nearly equivalent amounts of RNA polymerase II are associated with the TSS of all loci that were targeted by MGA in both the MGA-expressing and MGA-deleted KP cells.
source: We detect nearly equivalent amounts of RNA polymerase II associated with the TSS of all loci that were targeted by MGA in both the MGA-expressing and MGA-deleted KP cells (Figure 5G)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in a figure.

claim: Genes whose expression is increased upon MGA loss show higher levels of TSS-proximal RNA polymerase II in the MGA-deleted cells relative to the control cells with wild-type levels of MGA.
source: However, when we only bin genes whose expression is increased upon MGA loss, we observe higher levels of TSS-proximal RNA polymerase II in the MGA-deleted cells relative to the control cells with wild-type levels of MGA (Figure 5H)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in a figure.

claim: Genes whose expression is downregulated upon MGA deletion exhibit nearly the same relative levels of RNA polymerase II binding to the TSS, although the regions flanking the TSS show somewhat lower levels of polymerase in the sgMGA cells.
source: By contrast, genes whose expression is downregulated upon MGA deletion exhibit nearly the same relative levels of RNA polymerase II binding to the TSS, although the regions flanking the TSS show somewhat lower levels of polymerase in the sgMGA cells (Figure 5I)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in a figure.

claim: An overall decrease in MGA and L3MBTL2 binding was observed in MGA-inactivated A549 cells, including at STAG3 and PODXL2 promoters.
source: As for mouse KP lines, we observed a overall decrease in MGA and L3MBTL2 binding in MGA-inactivated cells (termed sgMGA), including at STAG3 and PODXL2 promoters (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; Supplementary file 1d)
evidence: The claim is supported by CUT and RUN data shown in a figure.

claim: Concomitant with an increase in STAG3 and PODXL2 expression in sgMGA A549 cells, there was decreased occupancy of MGA and L3MBTL2 at their respective promoters accompanied by an increase in MYC binding.
source: Concomitant with an increase in STAG3 and PODXL2 expression in sgMGA A549 cells, there was decreased occupancy of MGA and L3MBTL2 at their respective promoters accompanied by an increase in MYC binding (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C)
evidence: The claim is supported by CUT and RUN and expression data shown in figures.

claim: Amplification of MYC paralogs is rare in LUAD whether or not MGA is inactivated.
source: Analysis of this data indicated that amplification of MYC paralogs is rare in LUAD whether or not MGA is inactivated (e.g. 1/23 cases of MGA truncating or splice site mutations exhibited amplification of MYCL, while 7/460 cases with wild-type MGA had amplification of any MYC paralogs)
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA data.

claim: TCGA samples did not indicate significantly altered MYC family RNA levels in MGA mutant tumors compared with wild-type MGA tumors.
source: Moreover, TCGA samples did not indicate significantly altered MYC family RNA levels in MGA mutant tumors compared with wild-type MGA tumors (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA data shown in a figure.

claim: Deletion of MYC in sgMGA-KP and control KP tumor lines resulted in suppression of proliferation in both cases.
source: To ask whether the endogenously expressed MYC is critical for growth, we deleted MYC in sgMGA-KP and control KP tumor lines and found suppression of proliferation in both cases (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Treatment of control and sgMGA A549 cells with 10058-F4 revealed that MGA deficient cells are as sensitive to MYC inhibition as control vector-transduced cells.
source: In addition, treatment of control and sgMGA A549 cells with 10058-F4, an extensively used MYC-MAX dimerization inhibitor (Yin et al., 2003) revealed that MGA deficient cells are as sensitive to MYC inhibition as control vector-transduced cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure and citation.

claim: A similar trend is observed for A549 cells upon treatment with MS2-008, a chemical probe that inhibits MYC-MAX-driven transcription.
source: A similar trend is observed for A549 cells upon treatment with MS2-008 (Struntz et al., 2019), a chemical probe that inhibits MYC-MAX-driven transcription (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure and citation.

claim: Genes associated with meiotic recombination, repair or outgrowth are among the top 50 genes upregulated upon MGA loss as well as by reduction of PCGF6 or L3MBTL2 levels.
source: Most notably we find that genes associated with meiotic recombination, repair or outgrowth are among the top 50 genes upregulated upon MGA loss as well as by reduction of PCGF6 or L3MBTL2 levels (e.g. Stag3, Tdrkh, Zcwpw1, Gpc2) (Figure 6A,B)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in figures.

claim: For the majority of genes neither single inactivation of L3mbtl2, Pcgf6, nor CRISPR inactivation of both L3mbtl2 + Pcgf6, lead to upregulation to the same overall extent as the MGA deletion itself.
source: However, the data indicate that for the majority of genes neither single inactivation of L3mbtl2, Pcgf6, nor CRISPR inactivation of both L3mbtl2 + Pcgf6, lead to upregulation to the same overall extent as the MGA deletion itself
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data comparing different deletions.

claim: STAG3 appeared to be highly expressed (SD > 3 above mean) in a significant subset of MGA-altered cases (truncating mutations and deletions).
source: Interestingly, STAG3 appeared to be highly expressed (SD > 3 above mean) in a significant subset of MGA-altered cases (truncating mutations and deletions) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B)
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA data shown in figures.

claim: Genes overexpressed in the MGA-altered group are significantly enriched for MYC, MAX, E2F6, and E2F4 in Enrichr ChEA analysis.
source: Genes overexpressed in the MGA-altered group are significantly enriched for MYC, MAX, E2F6, and E2F4 in Enrichr ChEA analysis (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChEA analysis shown in a figure.

claim: There appeared to be a significant downregulation of anti-tumor immune responses and decrease in IFN signaling genes such as IFITM1 in MGA-altered cases.
source: Consistent with mouse Kras tumor data, there appeared to be a significant downregulation of anti-tumor immune responses and decrease in IFN signaling genes such as IFITM1 in MGA-altered cases (Figure 7A,B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA data shown in figures.

claim: Established ncPRC1.6 target STAG3 and pro-invasion gene PODXL2 were significantly altered in all three comparisons (mouse Kras, KP, and human TCGA).
source: Amongst the five gene overlap, we observed that established ncPRC1.6 target STAG3 and pro-invasion gene PODXL2 were significantly altered in all three comparisons (Figure 7C–E)
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis shown in figures.

claim: MGA suppression conferred no growth advantage to A549 and NCI-H23 lines, in contrast to the phenotypes observed in models where MGA was inactivated at the tumor initiation stage.
source: Interestingly, MGA suppression conferred no growth advantage to these lines, in contrast to the phenotypes we observed in models where MGA was inactivated at the tumor initiation stage (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F,H compare with Figure 1B,F, and l)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: An increase in invasive properties was observed upon MGA inactivation as evidenced by faster migration of MGA-inactivated cells in wound healing assays.
source: However, we observed an increase in invasive properties upon MGA inactivation as evidenced by faster migration of MGA-inactivated cells in wound healing assays (Figure 7F,G, Figure 7—figure supplement 1I,J)
evidence: The claim is supported by wound healing assay data shown in figures.

claim: A549 sgMGA cells formed less compact spheroids.
source: and formation of less compact spheroids by A549 sgMGA cells (Figure 7H,I)
evidence: The claim is supported by spheroid formation data shown in figures.

claim: An up-regulation of PODXL2 and STAG3 was observed in MGA-inactivated A549 cells.
source: In addition, we observed an up-regulation of PODXL2 and STAG3 (Figure 7J,K)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in figures.

claim: Knockdown of either STAG3 or PODXL2 led to a substantial reduction in cell growth and this effect was more pronounced in sgMGA cells.
source: Knockdown of either gene led to a substantial reduction in cell growth and this effect was more pronounced in sgMGA cells (Figure 7L)
evidence: The claim is supported by cell growth data shown in a figure.

claim: Neither loss of L3MBTL2 nor PCGF6 phenocopied the effects seen on migration in MGA CRISPR cells.
source: Neither loss of L3MBTL2 nor PCGF6 phenocopied the effects seen on migration (Figure 7—figure supplement 1N,O) in MGA CRISPR cells
evidence: The claim is supported by migration assay data shown in figures.

claim: MGA loss was accompanied by a decrease in L3MBTL2 levels in colon organoids, as observed in lung cancer models.
source: MGA loss was accompanied by a decrease in L3MBTL2 levels, as we had observed in our lung cancer models (Figure 8B, Figure 3B,D)
evidence: The claim is supported by protein level data shown in figures.

claim: Inactivation of MGA in colon organoids did not impact growth in 2D culture but clearly accelerated 3D growth over a period of 14 days.
source: Inactivation of MGA in colon organoids did not impact growth in 2D culture (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C) but clearly accelerated 3D growth over a period of 14 days (Figure 8C,D, Figure 8—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by organoid growth data shown in figures.

claim: Four of the five genes (STAG3, PODXL2, NHLRC1, and ZCWPW1) identified from analysis in lung cancer models were significantly upregulated upon loss of MGA in colon organoids.
source: Importantly, we observed that four of the five genes (STAG3, PODXL2, NHLRC1, and ZCWPW1) identified from our analysis in lung cancer models were significantly upregulated upon loss of MGA (Figure 8F, Supplementary file 1e)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in a figure.

claim: Similar to the mouse lung adenocarcinoma KP model, the expression of several EMT-related genes was elevated upon MGA loss in colon organoids.
source: Similar to the mouse lung adenocarcinoma KP model, the expression of several EMT-related genes was elevated upon MGA loss
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data comparing colon organoids to KP model.

claim: A broad upregulation of E2F regulated, cell cycle and DNA replication associated genes was noted upon MGA loss in colon organoids.
source: Strikingly, we also noted a broad upregulation of E2F regulated, cell cycle and DNA replication associated genes (Figure 8G)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in a figure.

claim: As in the Kras tumors, inflammation and interferon signaling genes were significantly enriched amongst the downregulated genes in colon organoids.
source: As in the Kras tumors, inflammation and interferon signaling genes were significantly enriched amongst the downregulated genes (Figure 8H)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in a figure.

claim: Several colon stemness associated genes including LGR5 were upregulated upon MGA loss in colon organoids.
source: For example, several colon stemness associated genes including LGR5 were upregulated upon MGA loss (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E; Muñoz et al., 2012; van der Flier et al., 2009)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in a figure and citations.

claim: Senescence appeared to be a major process enriched amongst the downregulated genes in colon organoids upon MGA loss.
source: Conversely, senescence appeared to be a major process enriched amongst the downregulated genes (Figure 8H, Figure 8—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in figures.

claim: MGA is a dual specificity transcription factor that contains both a TBX domain and a bHLHZ region.
source: MGA is unique in that it is a dual specificity transcription factor that contains both a TBX domain and a bHLHZ region (Hurlin et al., 1999)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Loss of MGA leads to peri-implantation lethality due to defects in polyamine biosynthesis.
source: Specifically, loss of MGA leads to peri-implantation lethality due to defects in polyamine biosynthesis (Washkowitz et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: MGA and its dimerization partner MAX are both involved in repressing germ cell-related transcripts.
source: An RNAi screen revealed that MGA and its dimerization partner MAX are both involved in repressing germ cell-related transcripts (Maeda et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: MGA and MAX act to prevent entry into meiosis in germline stem cells by directly repressing meiotic genes.
source: and act to prevent entry into meiosis in germline stem cells by directly repressing meiotic genes (Suzuki et al., 2016)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: MGA interacts with non-canonical PRC1.6 complexes in ES cells and plays an integral role in recruiting ncPRC1.6 members to target promoters.
source: Moreover, a number of studies have shown that MGA interacts with non-canonical PRC1.6 complexes (herein ncPRC1.6) in ES cells and plays an integral role in recruiting ncPRC1.6 members to target promoters (Fursova et al., 2019; Gao et al., 2012; Ogawa et al., 2002; Scelfo et al., 2019; Stielow et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Ectopic expression of MGA in lung adenocarcinoma cell lines retards their growth.
source: A recent study revealed that ectopic expression of MGA in lung adenocarcinoma cell lines retards their growth (Llabata et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: Enrichment in nonsense mutations at the MGA locus across all cancers is statistically significant, suggestive of a tumor suppressive role for the protein.
source: and enrichment in nonsense mutations at the MGA locus across all cancers is statistically significant, suggestive of a tumor suppressive role for the protein (ICGC Breast Cancer Group et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation and statistical analysis of mutation data.

claim: MGA emerged as one of the top hits in a genome-wide CRISPR screen for tumor suppressors in DLBCL lines.
source: Consistent with this, MGA emerged as one of the top hits in a genome-wide CRISPR screen for tumor suppressors in DLBCL (diffuse large B-cell lymphoma) lines (Reddy et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a CRISPR screen study.

claim: High STAG3 expression in colorectal cancer is associated with metastasis, drug resistance, and poor clinical outcomes.
source: That at least some of these genes are relevant to human cancer is supported by a recent report that high STAG3 expression in colorectal cancer is associated with metastasis, drug resistance, and poor clinical outcomes (Sasaki et al., 2021)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a recent report.

claim: MGA acts as a bona fide tumor suppressor in vivo.
